title: Finite-level proper and open projection factors with coefficient transport
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,\overline X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ an open immersion and $p_0:\overline X\to Y$ proper, and put $f=p_0j$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, and write $A_T$ for its constant ring sheaf on the small pro-étale site of $T$. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of $A_T$-module sheaves, K-flat derived tensor, exact inverse image with $u^{-1}A_T=A_{T'}$, and the canonical adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ and $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ and $B\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ have bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Define
$$\rho_{p_0}:Rp_{0,*}j_!C\otimes_A^LB\longrightarrow Rp_{0,*}(j_!C\otimes_A^Lp_0^{-1}B)$$
as the transpose of $\varepsilon_{j_!C}\otimes1$ under $p_0^{-1}\dashv Rp_{0,*}$, after the pullback/tensor identification. Define
$$\rho_j:j_!(C\otimes_A^Lj^{-1}p_0^{-1}B)\longrightarrow j_!C\otimes_A^Lp_0^{-1}B$$
as the transpose of $\eta_C\otimes1$ under $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$. Then both $\rho_{p_0}$ and $\rho_j$ are isomorphisms, natural in $C,B$, and $j_!C$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. The inverse of $\rho_j$ is the canonical open projection comparison $j_!C\otimes_A^LL\to j_!(C\otimes_A^Lj^{-1}L)$ at $L=p_0^{-1}B$.

Moreover, the exact section-action equivalence from internal modules over $p_T^*\underline A$ to ordinary $A_T$-modules [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence, lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] identifies the unbounded derived tensor products, all Tor intervals, and the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] with these ordinary ones. For finite $A$, the finite constant local models are precisely locally constant finite $A$-modules. Under its canonical operation comparisons, it identifies the derived adjunction units and counits, the two displayed projection maps and the compactification composite $Rp_{0,*}j_!$ in the internal and ordinary presentations. No algebraic closure or finiteness of $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: For the ordinary finite-level assertion, finite type over the field makes X, Z and Y Noetherian. Apply exceptionalTransport_constructible_comparison [new-etale-proetale-exceptional-object-comparison] to C and B. Convert explicit etale cohomology vanishing bounds to canonical t-structure boundedness, and use isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf to identify the two etale constructibility conventions. This gives C in the source bounded-constructible category with its original Tor interval, and a bounded etale origin B0 of B.

Apply the existing source theorem constructibleFiniteTor_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek to C and the quasi-compact open j. Translate bounded constructibility back to the intrinsic fixed-module convention using the comparison of the preceding step. Apply torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek to preserve the original ordered Tor interval [a,b]. This proves both admissibility conclusions for j!C, retaining the open-extension route of the unit. The adopted source proof reduces bounded constructibility and finite Tor to the etale open-extension theorem [lem-trf-open-ctf] via its fixed finite-coefficient comparison; it does not invoke the condensed localizing theorem.

Apply the existing source theorem isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_app_app_of_bounded (ProjectionFormulaBounded) to the proper p0, the same open j, C and B0. It already assembles the etale projection formula, comparison of the canonical projection maps, and the tensor cohomology bound from finite Tor amplitude of C. Transport its IsIso conclusion along the origin isomorphism comparison(B0) ≅ B by NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso. This uses neither finite Tor amplitude of B nor a field extension.

The source instance isIso_derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekProjectionMap gives invertibility of the actual open unit-transpose map for arbitrary inputs. derivedTensorOpenImmersionLowerShriekIso is its specified inverse; its inverse-hom identity and uniqueness of inverses prove the displayed inverse formula. Combine this with the preceding conclusions using conjunction introduction. Naturality is already encoded by the source bifunctor natural transformation.

For scalarMap_existsUnique and encoding_properties at the actual scalar universe, compose the constant-abelian-sheaf unit with the monoidal constantSchemeIso [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. Its compatibility with unit and multiplication makes its section maps ring homomorphisms. The sheafification adjunction extends this map uniquely to the reconstructed commutative section-ring sheaf. Forgetting to abelian sheaves identifies the extension, via constantCommuteCompose, with constantSchemeIso, so the ring map is invertible. Compose the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], restriction along the two ring isomorphisms, and the constant-ring restriction equivalence [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]. Restriction along a ring isomorphism has inverse restriction along its inverse, with identity component maps. All four factors retain the underlying additive maps, so their composite is additive. This construction uses A in Type (u+1) directly, without a scalar universe lift or a finite-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: For the retained internal-coefficient comparison clauses: Apply [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence] to the discrete finite ring $A$ on each scheme. The resulting exact unbounded derived equivalences identify $p_T^*\underline A$ with $A_T$, derived tensors and every Tor interval. By [lem-pe-finite-coefficient-model-comparison] they identify finite-constant-model constructibility with intrinsic finite-stalk constructibility, with the same cohomological intervals. The Noetherian-scheme hypothesis follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. All these schemes are also qcqs: quasi-compactness is part of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-separatedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. For the local models, a finitely presented $A$-module is finite since it is a quotient of a finite power of $A$; conversely a finite module has a presentation $A^r\twoheadrightarrow M$ whose kernel is finite and hence finitely generated. Thus its finite constant models are exactly locally constant finite $A$-modules.

For the retained internal-coefficient comparison clauses: Use [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] with $\Lambda=\underline A$. It identifies the actual derived pullbacks, direct images, open extensions, tensorators, and both adjunctions including units and counits with their ordinary ringed-topos versions. Consequently the proper transpose of $(\varepsilon_{j_!C}\otimes1)\circ\delta_{p_0}$ is carried to the displayed $\rho_{p_0}$. For the open map, its transpose is $\mu_j\circ(\eta_C\otimes1)$; the same comparison identifies each of these two factors, hence identifies its adjunct with the displayed $\rho_j$. Composing the operation comparisons identifies $Rp_{0,*}D(j_!)$ with $Rp_{0,*}j_!$. These are identifications of the specified maps, not just of their endpoints.

proof.text: For the retained internal-coefficient comparison clauses: Tensor, the adjunction bijections, and their units and counits are natural. Therefore the two maps defined in the statement are natural in $C,B$; the componentwise inverses of a natural isomorphism are natural by multiplying its naturality square by the two inverses. The comparisons of step 2 carry those same units, counits and tensorators, so also carry both projection maps, their inverses and their compactification composite. Together with steps 1 and 3 this proves every clause, without imposing any further assumption on $k$.
